extraction.document_summary: AIA Centurion PA is a personal accident insurance plan designed for “golden years”, offering worldwide coverage for accidental death, accidental injury, accidental disability and specified accident-related events. It has three basic benefit levels (Plan 1/Plan 2/Plan 3) with coverage amounts such as Accidental Death of S$30,000 / S$60,000 / S$100,000 and Accidental Medical Reimbursement of S$1,000 / S$2,000 / S$3,000. It also provides daily accidental hospital income (S$50 / S$100 / S$150), plus home-care and mobility/medical-related reimbursement amounts. Most benefits (except benefit #9, #12 and #13) are reduced by 50% from the policy anniversary on or after age 81. Coverage starts at age 40 up to age 80 (last birthday) and is described as continuing “till age 100”, with “guaranteed acceptance” described as “no health questions asked”. The optional Dementia Benefit adds multi-stage dementia coverage (Option 1/2/3) with early/intermediate paying 50% once and major stage paying 100% less the early/intermediate payout, for eligible dementia types until age 85.
quality_notes: Brochure provides plan tables with explicit coverage amounts and an optional dementia section with stage mechanics.
Some operational terms (e.g., exact benefit triggers/definition wording, renewal terms, and full exclusions) are not present beyond high-level notes and caveats.

policies.quick_summary: Personal accident insurance with worldwide coverage for accidental death/injury/disability and accident-related medical/reimbursement benefits, offered in Basic Plans 1–3, plus an optional multi-stage Dementia Benefit with reimbursement and stage-based payout mechanics (Early & Intermediate vs Major stage). Entry is described as age 40 to 80 (last birthday) with coverage “till age 100”, and “Guaranteed acceptance” is described as no health questions asked for the base plan. Most benefits reduce by 50% from policy anniversary on or after age 81 (except certain benefits). Public documentation lists multiple benefit amounts per plan tier.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Platinum AccidentCare is a personal accident plan designed to provide 24-hour protection for accidental deaths and injuries, with additional assistance and reimbursements. Core payouts are tied to a “coverage amount” and can reach up to 150% of that coverage amount for events listed in the “Schedule of Indemnity,” including “Permanent total disablement” (150% of coverage amount) and certain burn/disability outcomes. The plan also includes an “Aviation Accident Benefit” that pays an additional amount equal to the coverage amount when death occurs due to an injury sustained on a flight (double indemnity). In addition to lump sum benefits, it reimburses overseas emergency medical evacuation and repatriation (unlimited) and covers categories of medical expenses and supportive care (e.g., TCM/chiropractor, mobility aids/home modification after major disability, and rehabilitation therapy). Plans are offered as Silver (S$1,000,000 coverage), Gold (S$3,000,000), and Diamond (S$5,000,000) for the core accidental death/dismemberment/burns benefit; accidental medical reimbursement and mobility/home-modification limits scale by plan.
quality_notes: Brochure contains clear plan tables for Silver/Gold/Diamond and several named benefits with explicit limits and (where available) percentages.

Entry/maximum age, exact underwriting method, and many eligibility conditions are not stated in the provided text (only limited conditional notes are provided, e.g., age 75 reduction and a 50% claims condition for mobility aids/home modification).
Optional benefits include a weekly-income structure and a monthly support benefit; the monthly amount is shown for some plan columns but Diamond monthly amount is not clearly visible in the excerpt.

policies.quick_summary: Personal accident plan with core lump-sum payouts for accidental death, dismemberment and burns (up to 150% of coverage amount) plus aviation double indemnity, overseas emergency medical evacuation/repatriation (unlimited), and multiple reimbursement/support benefits (e.g., medical reimbursement, TCM/chiropractor, mobility aids/home modification, rehabilitation support, compassionate visit). Plans offered: Silver (S$1,000,000), Gold (S$3,000,000), Diamond (S$5,000,000) coverage amount for core benefits; accidental medical reimbursement and other sub-limits increase by plan. Certain benefits reduce by 50% at age 75.
coverage_scope: Accidental deaths and injuries
Accidental death, accidental dismemberment and burns (core benefit)

Medical expense reimbursements for specified treatments and nursing/ambulance services
TCM and chiropractor medical reimbursement (as a complementary benefit)
Mobility aids and home modification expenses after a major disability (subject to eligibility condition)
Rehabilitation support treatment expenses for therapists after a major disability (including TCM/chiropractor note is included under coverage description)
Compassionate visit travel/accommodation expenses for a relative/friend while insured is hospitalised overseas
Illness-related accidents coverage mentioned (e.g., dengue fever and food poisoning) and certain recreational sports mishaps (as described in brochure text)
policies.eligibility_notes: Mobility aids/home modification benefit eligibility: “total claims paid or payable due to 1 accident under Accidental Death, Accidental Dismemberment and Burns Benefit (other than for Loss of Life) must be at least 50% of the coverage amount.” Rehabilitation support is “upon a major disability.” Overseas references include “outside Singapore, your home country and your usual place of residence or employment.”

extraction.document_summary: AIA Prime Assured is a personal accident insurance plan providing worldwide accident protection (“anywhere in the world”). It pays benefits following an injury due to an accident, including (1) Compassionate Accidental Death (Plan 1/2/3 all S$5,000), (2) Broken Bones and Burns (S$10,000 / S$15,000 / S$30,000, paid using a schedule of percentages of the plan’s coverage amount), (3) Permanent Disability (S$20,000 / S$30,000 / S$50,000, using a disability schedule with stated percentage limits), (4) Daily Hospital Income (up to 365 days at S$50 / S$100 / S$150 per day), and (5) Accident Medical Reimbursement (up to 25% of the coverage amount per accident). Key limitation: most benefits’ coverage amount reduces by 50% from the policy anniversary following age 81, and Alzheimer’s/Parkinson’s pays only once during the policy life (regardless of renewal).
quality_notes: Plan 1/2/3 benefit amounts and premium amounts are clearly tabulated.
Broken Bones and Burns and Permanent Disability are given as percentage schedules of the coverage amount, with explicit aggregation caps.
No explicit general exclusions list is provided in this brochure (only a note that exclusions exist in the policy contract).

policies.quick_summary: Worldwide personal accident plan paying scheduled benefits for death, broken bones/burns, permanent disability, loss of ADLs, selected medical/hospital-related expenses, and Alzheimer’s/Parkinson’s disease (once per policy life). Most benefits are based on a coverage amount that reduces by 50% from the policy anniversary after age 81; Plan 1/2/3 set different coverage amounts and daily/per-accident benefit levels. Premiums are quoted as inclusive of 9% GST on annual/twice-yearly/monthly payment frequencies. Broken bones/burns and permanent disability payouts follow percentage schedules with explicit caps for multiple injuries/disabled events.

Broken Bones and Burns and Permanent Disability payments are subject to explicit caps for multiple injuries arising from the same accident and for policy-year aggregates.
Daily Accident Hospital Income Benefit pays up to 365 days.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Solitaire PA (II) is a personal accident insurance plan with extended coverage beyond personal accidents. It provides 24/7 worldwide coverage for medical and other treatment costs (including TCM and chiropractic), plus coverage for items such as food poisoning and transport/building-fire related incidents. The plan is offered with 4 levels of protection (Plan 1 to Plan 4) with base benefits including Accidental Death up to S$750,000 (Plan 4), and Accidental Permanent Total Disability up to S$2,250,000 (Plan 4). It also includes Accident Medical Reimbursement with Plan 4 shown at S$5,000. Optional benefits (on top of the selected basic plan tier) include Lifestyle Maintenance (e.g., Weekly Income Benefit up to S$400) and Accidental Hospitalisation benefits (e.g., Daily Accidental Hospital Income up to S$350). A key limitation/caveat: basic coverage amounts (except the Renewal Bonus) are reduced by 50% at 75 years old, and optional benefits terminate at 75 years old; coverage is stated to be payable upon occurrence of an accident, and optional benefits have the same selected-or-lower plan type requirement.
quality_notes: The brochure clearly lists the 4 plan tiers and their base and optional benefit amounts.
No explicit exclusions were provided in the supplied text (only a general statement that exclusions exist in the policy contract).
The document does not state detailed underwriting rules beyond 'no medical check-up required'.
Benefit payout mechanics (e.g., deductibles/waiting periods, claim limits, survival periods) are not described in the supplied excerpt.

policies.quick_summary: AIA Solitaire PA (II) is AIA’s personal accident plan with worldwide coverage that extends to medical (including TCM and chiropractic), food poisoning and certain incident types (e.g., transport accidents/building fires). It has 4 protection levels (Plan 1–Plan 4) with base benefits such as Accidental Death (S$100,000 to S$750,000) and Accident Medical Reimbursement (S$2,000 to S$5,000). It also offers optional benefits for lifestyle maintenance and accidental hospitalisation. Basic benefit amounts (other than the Renewal Bonus) reduce by 50% at age 75, and optional benefits terminate at age 75.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Star Protector Plus is an accident and health protection plan for children from 2 weeks old, with coverage “till age 75.” It provides “comprehensive 5-point coverage” including (1) an “Accidental Death, Accidental Dismemberment and Burns Benefit,” (2) a “Monthly Catastrophe Cash Benefit (Accident)” that pays monthly up to 20 years if catastrophic disability occurs within 180 days of the accident, (3) “Medical Reimbursement Benefit (Accident & Disease)” for specified medical items, (4) “Daily Hospital Income Benefit (Accident & Disease)” up to a stated number of days, and (5) “Post-Hospitalisation Home Care Benefit (Accident & Disease).” Plan tiers are Plan 1/2/3 with different coverage amounts and hospital income rates (e.g., Daily Hospital Income: 30/day, 50/day, 100/day; Medical Reimbursement: 1,500, 3,000, 5,000). There is also an optional “Child Critical Illnesses Benefit” (Option 1/2/3: coverage amounts 30,000 / 50,000 / 100,000), convertible at the child’s adulthood, and it terminates on the policy anniversary following the child’s 21st birthday. A key limitation/caveat stated is that “waiting period and deferment period are applicable before the benefits will be payable,” and only up to 150% of the coverage amount may be paid for injuries arising from the same accident.
quality_notes: Document contains clear plan tables for Plan 1/2/3 and Optional Benefit options, plus a Schedule of Indemnity and specific benefit mechanics (ICU double indemnity, durations, reimbursement sub-limits).
Some underwriting/eligibility details (e.g., medical underwriting method) and key policy mechanics (e.g., free-look, grace period) are not stated explicitly.

policies.quick_summary: Worldwide accident and health protection for children (entry from 2 weeks to 16 years; coverage till age 75), with Plan 1/2/3 basic benefits including accidental death/dismemberment/burns, catastrophe monthly cash, medical reimbursement, daily hospital income (including ICU double indemnity), and post-hospitalisation home care. It also includes education assurance fund and multiple accident/disease reimbursement components; a separate optional Child Critical Illnesses Benefit (Option 1/2/3) can be converted and terminates after age 21. Waiting and deferment periods apply before benefits become payable.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Absolute Critical Cover is a critical illness protection plan that also extends to “every stage” of covered conditions, including early, intermediate and major stage critical illnesses, as well as chronic diseases, age-related conditions, and “future unknown diseases”. Buyers can choose a coverage term “up to age 65, 75, or 100”. The plan pays (i) critical illness benefits for covered conditions (including named examples such as thyroid disorders and sleep apnoea), (ii) an additional Safety Net Cover payout if admitted to ICU for at least 4 days—equal to 20% of the coverage amount on top of existing coverage, with a cap described for this benefit, and it terminates thereafter, and (iii) potential cash value only when the term is “up to age 100” via surrender and maturity benefits (75% of coverage amount; maturity at age 100 is 150% of coverage amount). A key caveat is that claims under the Critical Illness Benefit reduce surrender/maturity benefits, and there are stated exclusions such as pre-existing conditions with waiting/survival periods.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Beyond Critical Care is a critical illness (CI) protection plan with multistage CI coverage, relapse protection, and additional benefits for mental well-being. Under the base plan, it covers 43 major stage critical illnesses and 5 rediagnosed or recurred critical illnesses, paying 100% of the coverage amount as a lump sum upon first diagnosis, with the coverage amount restored to 100% after 12 months (subject to the rules on same vs different rediagnosed/recurred events). It also adds mental well-being benefit for 5 mental illnesses, paying an additional 20% of the coverage amount (up to S$50,000 per claim) until age 75, with up to 5 claims (S$150,000 total across all policies). The plan includes a 100% premium refund at policy expiry (base plan total annual premiums, less claims and amounts owing), but exclusions apply for pre-existing conditions and the brochure notes waiting and survival periods before benefits are payable.
quality_notes: Brochure clearly states many core benefit mechanics (payout percentages, coverage counts, refund mechanics, and several caps).
Specific rider product summary details (full CI lists/definitions under each rider) are not provided in this excerpt; only rider names and some waiver mechanics are stated.
Waiting/survival periods are mentioned generally, but exact durations for each benefit are not consistently specified in the excerpt.

Riders mentioned include multistage CI cover extra and premium waiver/payor benefits triggered by specified CI/mental illness events (details vary by rider). Pre-existing conditions are excluded; waiting and survival periods apply before benefits are payable; some coverage restoration/claim rules depend on whether the subsequent claim is the same or different event.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Diabetes Care is a critical illness insurance plan targeted at Type 2 diabetics and pre-diabetics. It is designed to provide easier access: eligibility is stated as requiring the insured to be a non-smoker with diabetes diagnosed after age 25 and no pre-existing diabetes-related complications, and the brochure says coverage access is possible “without the need for medical examinations” by answering “5 simple questions”. The core protection covers five diabetes-related critical illnesses (blindness, coronary artery bypass surgery, specified-severity heart attack, end stage kidney failure, and stroke with permanent neurological deficit) with a payout of either the full coverage amount or “110% of the total annual premiums paid”, whichever is higher. Coverage is “guaranteed renewable” and the premium remains “the same throughout the whole policy, up to age 80”. It also pays an extra 20% of the coverage amount for specified diabetes-related limb amputation (one-time, and only if no critical illness benefit payout has been made). An optional Cancer Cover rider can add 20% for early/intermediate cancer and a further 100% for major cancer, subject to one-time payout conditions.
quality_notes: The brochure provides clear descriptions of key covered events and payout mechanics.
Age range is stated for eligibility (30 to 65) and premium guarantee is stated up to age 80, but full policy term details and exact waiting/survival periods are not provided.
No specific numeric annual/lifetime limits are stated in the brochure.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Enhanced Cancer Protect is a cancer protection plan that provides payouts from the first cancer diagnosis through up to two major stage cancer relapses. The brochure states coverage of up to S$700,000, with each relapse claimable two years apart, and premiums that do not change yearly “1” (premiums are set by entry age and may be adjusted later). Buyers can choose a coverage period of 20 years or “till 65 years old”. The core mechanics are: (1) first diagnosis payout at 100% of the coverage amount, (2) 1st and 2nd major-stage relapse payouts at 100% each, and (3) optional Enhanced Cancer Protect Plus add-on that increases total coverage up to 400%, adds early-stage (50% payout) and catastrophic cancer coverage, and shows an example where catastrophic cancer triggers an additional payout while the 2nd relapse benefit also pays.
quality_notes: Document provides clear benefit mechanics for first diagnosis, two relapse claims (two years apart), and optional add-on early/catastrophic coverage via worked examples and diagrams.
Exact definitions of covered “Major Cancer”, “Intermediate/Stage”, and “catastrophic cancer” are not enumerated in detail; only a list of early-stage cancers is provided.
No explicit sum-assured range table or entry/maximum ages are stated beyond coverage ending at age 65 or after 20 years.
Underwriting type, medical exam requirement, grace period, and free-look period are not stated.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Glow of Life is an AIA Singapore Private Limited critical illness plan designed specifically for women’s health needs and female-related critical illnesses. It provides a payout based on a “Female Dreaded Illness Benefit” for female cancers (including cancers of breast, cervix uteri, uterus, ovary, fallopian tube and vaginal/vulva), systemic lupus erythematosus (S.L.E) with lupus nephritis, and rheumatoid arthritis. It also includes a “Female Health Benefit” for osteoporosis (30% of coverage amount), urinary incontinence requiring surgical repair (5%), and carcinoma-in-situ of the female organs (20%), plus reconstructive surgery reimbursement due to accidents or burns (100%). Plans are tiered as Standard (S$25,000 coverage amount) and Executive (S$50,000). A second opinion on cancer is “Yes” for both. The brochure states a free health check-up once every two policy years (first available on the 3rd policy year), and a renewal bonus of 5% of the coverage amount for each renewal up to a maximum of five years. It also states that pre-existing conditions may result in no benefits and waiting periods apply for some conditions, with precise terms in the policy contract.
quality_notes: Premium table is present but benefit mechanics beyond percentages (e.g., exact waiting periods, definitions, limits/caps for reimbursement) are not provided in full.

extraction.document_summary: AIA HealthShield Gold Max is an AIA integrated shield plan (MediShield Life plus an additional private insurance coverage portion) designed to cover hospitalisation and many related inpatient/outpatient costs. It is offered with three plan tiers for ward entitlements: Max A (private standard ward or lower), Max B (A-class ward or lower), and Max B Lite (4-bedder or B1-class ward or lower). The brochure states high limits including “up to S$2 million per year” and “unlimited lifetime claim amount”, plus “guaranteed lifetime coverage.” Key mechanics include deductibles and co-insurance for eligible hospital bills and extended pre-/post-hospitalisation coverage (up to 13 months before/after hospitalisation, subject to the plan type). It also adds outpatient cancer benefits and a separate “extra cover for 30 critical illnesses per policy year” (up to S$100,000 for Max A; S$75,000 Max B; S$50,000 Max B Lite). A material caveat is that certain benefits are payable only on the plan’s stated ward/conditions (e.g., overseas treatment and specific outpatient limits) and the brochure notes that some exclusions apply (full list in policy contracts).
quality_notes: Brochure provides extensive benefit tables and explicit numeric limits by plan tier (Max A / Max B / Max B Lite and Standard plan for public hospitals).
Riders/add-ons are explicitly named as “add-on” (AIA Max VitalHealth Pro) and “Optional” add-ons within it (Cancer Care Pro, Emergency Care Pro).
Some underwriting/eligibility fields (entry age range, residency requirements, occupation classes, underwriting method) are not stated.
Some coverage mechanics reference footnotes (pre-existing conditions, pro-ration, deductible/co-insurance structure), but do not fully quantify every scenario in this brochure excerpt.
No explicit premium amounts are provided; premium-related fields are mostly described qualitatively (e.g., “no premium increase after claims”, “premium capped/co-payment” for add-on).

extraction.document_summary: AIA Hospital Income is a hospital cash plan intended to pay a daily cash allowance during hospitalisation and recovery to cover “unexpected extras” that may not be fully covered by your existing hospitalisation plan. It pays different cash benefits based on where/when the insured event occurs: a Daily Hospital Income Benefit of S$100/day (Plan 1), S$200/day (Plan 2), or S$300/day (Plan 3) up to 500 days; an Intensive Care Unit Income Benefit (on top of Daily Hospital Income) of S$300/day (Plan 1), S$450/day (Plan 2), or S$750/day (Plan 3) up to 30 days; and additional recovery supports such as Get Well Benefit, Post-hospitalisation Home Rest (up to 5 days), and Day Surgery Income Benefit. Premiums vary by entry age and plan, and the brochure states premium rates are not guaranteed.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Mum2Baby Choices is a prenatal protection proposition with guaranteed lifelong protection for the child, starting from as early as the 13th week of pregnancy. It is offered via two bundled base options: AIA Mum2Baby Protect (a participating whole life plan with boosted protection and stable cash value) and AIA Mum2Baby (an investment-linked plan that bolsters protection during early years and supports investment growth later). Both bundles cover the mother and baby for defined events, including pregnancy complications, childbirth-related medical negligence, congenital illnesses, and hospitalisation benefits. A key mechanic is that the prenatal base plan and applicable riders can be transferred to the child within 100 days from birth “with no medical questions asked,” and coverage is stated as guaranteed up to age 100.
quality_notes: Document provides clear benefit names, payout amounts tied to coverage amount, and stated timeframes (13th week, 100 days transfer, age 100).
Initial underwriting requirements for purchase of the base policy/riders are not explicitly stated; only the transfer is described as without medical questions.
No specific exclusion list is provided; only a generic statement that some conditions result in no benefits payable.

policies.quick_summary: AIA Mum2Baby Protect is a participating whole life prenatal bundle under AIA Mum2Baby Choices. It provides protection for the expectant mother and baby from as early as the 13th week of pregnancy and includes benefits for pregnancy complications, childbirth medical negligence, congenital illnesses, hospitalisation (up to 30 days), and major hospitalisation for mum. A Baby Protect Plus (III) prenatal rider can be transferred to the child within 100 days from birth with no medical questions asked, aiming at guaranteed coverage for the child up to age 100. Coverage amount options are S$5,000, S$10,000 or S$25,000, which drive the stated benefit payouts.

policies.quick_summary: AIA Mum2Baby is the investment-linked bundle under AIA Mum2Baby Choices. It provides prenatal protection for mother and baby beginning as early as the 13th week of pregnancy, with benefits including pregnancy complications, childbirth medical negligence, congenital illnesses, hospitalisation (up to 30 days) for both mum and baby, and a major hospitalisation care benefit for mum. Like the whole life bundle, the base plan and applicable riders can be transferred to the child within 100 days from birth with no medical questions asked, aiming for guaranteed lifelong coverage up to age 100. Coverage amount options are S$5,000, S$10,000 or S$25,000, which drive the stated daily hospitalisation rates and the lump-sum benefits.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Pay Protector is an AIA Singapore disability income insurance plan designed to provide fixed monthly income payouts when disability disrupts employment. The brochure states it pays a fixed monthly income for up to 5 years to help supplement loss of earnings, and it highlights that the monthly payout is not reduced by earnings or future changes to income. There is a 90-day deferment period mentioned in the benefits-at-a-glance section, and premiums are waived during the monthly income payout period (or until recovery, whichever is earlier). The plan is linked with AIA Vitality for premium discounts of up to 15% (capped at 15%, eligible from the second policy year onwards and only for members aged 16+), though the discount is not applied to loading-related extra premiums. An example illustrates that a S$3,000 monthly payout could total S$180,000 over 60 months.
quality_notes: The document is largely marketing/illustration content; core contractual details such as exact definitions of covered disability and explicit exclusion lists are not provided.
It mentions 'Choice of five affordable plans' but does not list the five plan names/tiers or the full set of coverage options.
Only one explicit coverage amount (S$1,000 monthly income payout) has premium rates shown (for 30-year-old non-smoker, occupational class 1), and higher payout plan options are not enumerated.

Coverage is described as applicable even for temporary/less severe disabilities and mental illnesses, but formal definitions/exclusions are not included in the brochure text provided here.

Stated example: S$3,000 monthly income payout for up to 5 years (S$3,000 x 60 months = S$180,000). Premium example provided for S$1,000 monthly income payout: S$18/month (30-year-old male) and S$26/month (30-year-old female), for non-smoker, occupational class 1.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Platinum International Health is a worldwide (excluding USA) international medical insurance plan with lifetime global medical coverage and high overall limits. The brochure states maximum claim limits of S$750,000 per policy year and S$5,000,000 per lifetime for Plan 1, versus S$1,500,000 per policy year and S$10,000,000 per lifetime for Plan 2, with “Maximum coverage period: Lifetime.” Reimbursement is generally “as charged” for many hospital items, but the plan requires choosing one deductible/co-insurance option: Option 1 (deductible S$1,500; co-insurance 10%, capped at S$15,000 per policy year) or Option 2 (deductible S$3,000; co-insurance 15%, capped at S$20,000 per policy year). It covers hospital, pre- (up to 90 days) and post-hospitalisation (up to 90 days), outpatient day surgery, emergency accidental outpatient treatment (within 24 hours of accident, up to 30 days), plus capped benefits for items such as outpatient dialysis (S$300,000/year) and proton beam therapy (S$100,000/year). Key caveats stated include exclusions for pre-existing conditions and an illness waiting period of at least 30 days.
quality_notes: Product name, territorial scope, lifetime limit, and core benefit caps are clearly stated in tables.
Deductible/co-insurance options (Option 1/Option 2) are stated, but the document does not explicitly link which deductible option must be paired with Plan 1 vs Plan 2.
Some benefits are listed as 'as charged' and caps are provided for certain therapies/treatments; the brochure does not state a universal claims methodology beyond deductible/co-insurance.
Important underwriting/eligibility details (e.g., entry age, renewal, medical underwriting type) are not provided.

Brochure states exclusions for pre-existing conditions and an illness waiting period of at least 30 days.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Premier Disability Cover is an income-protection disability insurance plan that pays monthly benefits tied to the insured’s pre-disability earnings. It provides a monthly benefit of up to 75% of existing income, paid starting from the end of a 60-day deferment period, and continues for up to 2 years; if the insured cannot perform any suitable occupation they were taught, experienced, or trained for after 2 years, payments continue until age 65 or recovery (whichever comes first). It also reimburses rehabilitation expenses up to 6x the monthly benefit per disability, pays a catastrophic disability benefit of 24x the monthly benefit (payable only once per policy), and pays a death benefit of 12x the monthly benefit for standalone policies. A payback benefit of up to 2x the monthly benefit helps during the 60-day deferment period, and premiums are waived up to age 65 or until recovery while monthly benefits continue. The brochure states exclusions apply, but does not detail them.
quality_notes: Document describes the product and key payout mechanics (monthly benefit, deferment reimbursement, rehabilitation, catastrophic disability, death benefit, and premium waiver).
Eligibility/entry age, duration of policy/renewal, and underwriting details are not stated.
Exclusions are mentioned generally, but specific exclusion conditions are not provided in the brochure text.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Protect 3 is a critical illness insurance plan designed to cover Singapore’s top 3 critical illnesses—Cancer, Heart Attack, and Stroke—with coverage split into early, intermediate, and major stages. The plan also adds a gender-specific benefit for major stage gender-specific cancers from the 3rd policy year. Buyers choose a coverage level of S$100K, S$200K, or S$300K and the coverage is stated to continue up to age 85. A key payout mechanic is a one-time claim-free cashback of 25% of the coverage amount paid on the policy anniversary on or after age 65, or 15 years from policy start, whichever is later. For major stage gender cancers, the brochure illustrates a base major stage critical illness benefit of S$300,000 plus an additional 15% (S$45,000) for a total of S$345,000. The brochure states “simple sign-ups, no medical checks” (via answering 4 questions) and that value-added medical services are not contractual benefits.
quality_notes: Payout mechanics are partially quantified: cashback (25%) and the gender-specific major stage cancer add-on (15%) are explicit; base CI stage payout amounts for early/intermediate are not stated.
Exclusions are mentioned only generically (e.g., pre-existing conditions), but specific excluded circumstances are not listed.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Ultimate Critical Cover (UCC) is a Singapore life insurance critical illness plan that provides multi-stage critical illness protection across early, intermediate and major stages, with a “Ultimate Reset Benefit” that resets coverage to 100% of the coverage amount every 12 months after the last critical illness claim. The brochure states “unlimited claims” applies to major-stage critical illnesses, with only one claim payable per stage and the total across all stages of the same critical illness capped at 100% of the coverage amount. For early and intermediate stages, it describes a maximum claim limit of 500% of coverage amount across early/intermediate stage claims, and eligibility is “covered for 150 medical conditions” across stages. The policy terminates after the death or accidental death benefit is paid. Riders mentioned include an enhancer (Ultimate Relapse Benefit and Catastrophic Critical Illness Benefit) and optional premium waiver/payor benefit riders that waive future premiums upon specified diagnoses or death/disability.
quality_notes: Brochure contains clear core mechanics (unlimited claims for major stage, Ultimate Reset Benefit, relapse and catastrophic benefits via an enhancer, and death/accidental death payouts).
Exact entry age limits, premium terms/frequencies, underwriting basis, and detailed exclusions are not specified in a structured way; exclusions are described only generically.

The list of covered critical illnesses is provided by table, but individual benefit amounts for each condition are not itemized beyond specific notes (e.g., Angioplasty cap and relapse waiting period).

Coverage term can be selected up to age 65, 75, or 85. Ultimate Relapse and Catastrophic Critical Illness features are described as an enhancer/add-on for UCC customers (not part of base benefits). Only one claim per stage and stage/coverage caps apply; policy terminates after death or accidental death payout is made, and a relapse rider has a 2-year waiting period described in the brochure terms section (rider linkage). Pre-existing conditions are mentioned as excluded with no benefit payable.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Guaranteed Protect Plus (IV) is a long-term life insurance plan that provides death and total & permanent disability (TPD) protection, with a “multiplier” feature to boost coverage up to 5 times. You can choose a multiplier cut-off age of 65 or 75; after that cut-off, the coverage amount is reduced back to the basic coverage amount (e.g., 5X coverage ends and returns to S$100,000 in the example). Protection also includes accumulated cash value with potential (non-guaranteed) bonuses. Premiums can be paid for a limited term of 15, 20 or 25 years, after which benefits continue. The plan also offers options during events: defer premiums for 12 consecutive months upon involuntary retrenchment, and an Income Drawdown Facility that lets you take 50% or 100% of coverage as cash value into annual payouts for 10 years. AIA Vitality integration may add “PowerUp Dollar” free additional coverage (up to 37.5%).
quality_notes: Brochure contains sufficient structural information on base benefits (death, TPD), multiplier mechanics, premium term choices, cash value/bonuses, and event-based options (premium deferral, income drawdown).

Some mechanics refer to other product summaries (e.g., critical illness lists and exclusions) without reproducing full details here, so critical illness benefit conditions cannot be fully extracted as covered_conditions.
No explicit free-look period, grace period, or exact guaranteed cash value schedule is stated; only general statements about cash value and non-guaranteed bonuses appear.

The plan includes premium discount and PowerUp Dollar rules tied to AIA Vitality; amounts are described in terms of percentages/caps but not as a standalone payable benefit amount within the base product section.

policies.quick_summary: Long-term life insurance with death and TPD protection, boosted via a coverage multiplier (up to 5X) with a cut-off age of 65 or 75, plus accumulated cash value and potential bonuses. Offers limited-payment premiums (15/20/25 years) and event-based options such as premium deferral for 12 months (upon involuntary retrenchment) and an Income Drawdown Facility (50% or 100% of coverage into 10 annual cash payouts). Coverage reduces after the multiplier cut-off age and death/TPD cease at specified ages (death to 100, TPD to 70). Eligibility integration with AIA Vitality may provide additional free coverage via PowerUp Dollar (up to 150% of base PowerUp Dollar).

extraction.document_summary: AIA Pro Lifetime Protector (II) is an AIA Investment-linked Plan (ILP) that combines protection with wealth accumulation. It provides death coverage and protection against disability plus “150 multi-stage critical illnesses”. The brochure also highlights that “Guaranteed protection for the first 10 years” means the policy and any unit-deducting riders “will not lapse for the first 10 years… regardless of investment performance” (if regular premiums are fully paid and no withdrawals are made). Critical illness and disability protection is enhanced via optional riders, including Total Disability Accelerator (II) (paying up to “100% of basic coverage amount” for total and permanent disability, ending at age 70) and Lifetime Critical Cover rider with a Power Reset feature. Power Reset can restore coverage to “100%… if this rider is still in force for 12 months” after the latest diagnosed (or relapsed) critical illness and can support multiple claims “up to 300% of your coverage amount”. Investment guidance is provided via Mercer Guided Portfolios (Pro Adventurous, Pro Balanced, Pro Cautious).

extraction.document_summary: DIRECT - AIA Term Cover is a Direct Purchase Insurance term life product from AIA Singapore Private Limited that provides cost-effective, flexible term protection without a savings/investment feature. It offers cover for Death, Terminal Illness, and Total and Permanent Disability (TPD), paying out the “coverage amount.” Buyers can select a coverage term (the brochure mentions premiums staying unchanged for 5 years, 20 years, or up to age 65). For renewals, the brochure states “guaranteed renewability for the 5-year term plan regardless of your health condition,” with the “last renewal age for the 5-year term” at age 80, and “protection up to age 85.” A 30-year-old male non-smoker example is given: about S$0.33/day for S$100,000 cover (illustrative, not a guaranteed rate). An optional Critical Illness rider can be added, with coverage for Critical Illness up to age 65. The plan has a 14-day free-look period.
quality_notes: Brochure text provides high-level mechanics (events covered, renewal ages, critical illness rider existence) but does not provide benefit trigger definitions, detailed payout amounts/limits for each event beyond “coverage amount,” or explicit underwriting/eligibility criteria.
Several numeric items are illustrated rather than stated as general product limits (e.g., the S$0.33/day example).

extraction.document_summary: DIRECT - AIA WHOLE LIFE COVER (II) is AIA’s Direct Purchase Insurance whole life plan that provides protection for life against Death and Terminal Illness up to age 100. If Death or Terminal Illness occurs, and also for Total and Permanent Disability (up to age 65), the insurer pays the insured amount together with any bonuses (if accrued). Premiums are designed to be affordable because you only pay up to age 70 or up to age 85, while the basic cover continues up to age 100. The policy may participate in annual non-guaranteed discretionary bonuses; once credited, annual bonuses form part of guaranteed benefits, and a potential one-off terminal bonus may be paid on claim, maturity, or surrender. A Critical Illness rider is optional, and it also lasts up to age 100.
quality_notes: Brochure provides clear product structure (whole life base + optional Critical Illness rider) and key payout events (Death/Terminal Illness/TPD up to age 65; maturity).
No numeric pricing, sum assured ranges, entry/maximum ages, waiting/free-look/grace periods, or underwriting type are stated in the document.
Bonus mechanics are described qualitatively but not with specific guaranteed rates; amounts are therefore not extracted.

extraction.document_summary: AIA Around the World Plus (II) is a travel insurance plan from AIA that provides “enhanced protection” before, during, and after trips, including COVID-19-related coverage. It is “one-size-fits-all” and lets you select coverage options, with “three levels of protection” and either “a single trip or a year of unlimited travel”, plus “an individual or family plan.” Coverage areas can be selected as ASEAN, Asia, or worldwide. Two named plan types are shown: Premier Deluxe and Classic. For example, Travel Cancellation reimbursements are S$15,000 (Premier Deluxe) vs S$5,000 (Classic), and Medical Expenses Overseas are up to S$2,000,000 (Premier Deluxe) vs S$200,000 (Classic) for children. The brochure also states COVID-19 benefits are payable on an additional basis and “none of them offset the payment of any other benefits,” with limits that vary by age and plan.
quality_notes: The brochure provides a detailed benefits table with plan-specific sums for Premier Deluxe and Classic.
COVID-19 benefits are clearly separated in the table and include an additional-basis and no-offset note.

review_notes: Only named base plan tiers (Premier Deluxe and Classic) are represented as plans; no separate marketed product names beyond these two are created.

COVID-19 Benefits are treated as part of the base policy benefits table (not as separate rider records) because the brochure does not label them as a rider/attachment; benefit_level is marked as optional within benefits only to distinguish them from non-COVID benefits in the brochure table context.

Some table rows show additional column values (e.g., 120,000 / 500,000) that are not explicitly labeled as a third plan in the excerpt; only Premier Deluxe and Classic are extracted as plan tiers per the brochure’s named plan columns. extraction.document_summary: AIA Elite HomeCare is a home insurance plan (with building and household contents cover) that also extends protection to certain events worldwide when you travel. It is described as a “first-loss policy”, so the brochure states AIA will compensate accordingly if the home is not insured for its full value. Cover is offered in three named tiers: Standard, Comprehensive, and Executive. For example, Building coverage is S$80,000 (Standard), S$120,000 (Comprehensive) and S$260,000 (Executive), while Contents coverage is S$16,000 / S$24,000 / S$37,000. The plan also provides worldwide personal liability up to S$500,000 across all tiers, and Worldwide Accidental Death benefit of S$20,000 (with Double Indemnity for Accidental Death of S$40,000 for certain causes within the building). Worldwide medical reimbursement for accidents is shown as S$250 across tiers, and a “5-Year Premium Waiver” is indicated as “Yes” for all tiers if Death/TPD occurs.
quality_notes: The brochure provides a clear tier table for Standard/Comprehensive/Executive with many specific benefit limits and sub-limits.
Some benefit-limit values are embedded in fragmented table formatting; nonetheless, the numeric amounts and tier mapping are mostly explicit.
Eligibility for the medical reimbursement/accidental death benefit is explicitly described as age-based for the insured and spouse/legal child.

policies.quick_summary: Home insurance with building and contents coverage, extended worldwide items/accidents/travel-related benefits, plus worldwide personal liability, accidental death and medical reimbursement, and a 5-year premium waiver option after Death/Total Permanent Disability. Offered in Standard, Comprehensive, and Executive tiers with different building/contents limits and an indicated annual premium per tier (inclusive of 9% GST). Described as a first-loss policy with compensation adjusted for underinsurance (no penalty for underinsurance). Deductibles apply on most claims except specified categories (e.g., fire and certain accident benefits).

extraction.document_summary: FWD Life PA is a guaranteed renewable personal accident insurance plan that provides lifetime coverage up to age 100, as long as premiums are paid on time. It centres on an Accidental Death and Disability Benefit (ADDB) with three base sum insured options: S$100,000, S$200,000, and S$500,000. Depending on the accident outcome, it can pay 100% of the ADDB sum insured for accidental death, and for accidental permanent disability it pays up to 150% of the ADDB sum insured. It can also provide multiple indemnities (double and triple) when accidental death/permanent disability occurs in specified transport/travel situations. The plan includes a Compassionate Grant Benefit (10% of ADDB) and accident-related inpatient/outpatient medical expense reimbursement (up to S$2,000 / S$3,000 / S$4,000 per accident), expiring at age 80. Optional riders include a Catch-All Rider (extra 10% of ADDB if ICU stay with invasive life support lasts 120+ consecutive hours) and an Income Support Rider offering Plan A/B/C daily hospital income (S$100/S$150/S$300 per day up to 365 days; halved for certain groups) and weekly income (S$100/S$200/S$350 per week up to 104 weeks; halved for certain groups; expires at age 75).
quality_notes: Most core benefit amounts and rider Plan A/B/C payout tables are stated clearly.
The brochure does not reliably state min/max entry age, policy term, or underwriting type (full/simplified/etc.).
Exclusions are mentioned generally, but specific exclusion list items are not provided in the supplied text.
APDB payout is referenced as dependent on a Permanent Disability Schedule in the policy contract; exact schedule amounts are not included.

extraction.document_summary: FWD Life PA is a guaranteed renewable personal accident insurance plan underwritten by FWD Singapore Pte. Ltd. Coverage is guaranteed renewability “until the person insured reaches age 100” as long as premiums are paid on time. The base structure is built around 3 plan types linked to ADDB (Accidental Death and Disability Benefit) sum insured of S$100,000 / S$200,000 / S$500,000, with Accidental Death (100% of ADDB sum insured) and Accidental Permanent Disability (up to 150% of ADDB sum insured). It also provides Double and Triple Indemnity on accidental death/permanent disability in defined travel/transport scenarios, plus Compassionate Grant (10% of ADDB sum insured). It pays inpatient and outpatient accident-related medical expenses (per accident limits) with sub-limits for Chinese physician/acupuncturist/bonesetter/chiropractor and physiotherapy, expiring when the person insured turns age 80. Optional riders include a Catch-All ICU add-on (extra 10% of ADDB) and Income Support Rider (daily/weekly hospital income with plan-specific amounts and age/group halving rules).
quality_notes: Product name, core benefits, plan types, and rider benefit mechanics are stated with numeric limits and explicit age/expiry conditions.
Underwriting method, entry age limits, grace period, free-look period, surrender/cash value details are only partially provided (free-look is mentioned; other items are not).
Exclusions are referenced only generically; no specific excluded causes/conditions are listed.

Optional riders add ICU-based extra 10% and daily/weekly hospital income for accidental hospitalization/temporary total disability with plan-specific rates and halving rules for certain groups/ages (as stated). Lifetime 10% No Claim Discount applies to premiums (incl. riders, if applicable). Coverage is guaranteed renewable until age 100 as long as premiums are paid on time.

extraction.document_summary: FWD MultiCover CI is a critical illness protection plan that provides multiple payouts and continued coverage beyond the first critical illness claim. It offers a “Critical Illness Benefit” with stage-based payouts (including early-/intermediate-stage and late-stage diagnoses) and continued protection for recurrence, with a “Critical Illness Booster Benefit” and limits on how much can be claimed cumulatively (including a shared 600% claim limit). For late-stage cases, policyholders may also exercise an “Accelerated Care Option” (75% of the Sum Insured) when conditions are met; this option can be exercised only once and is irreversible, and exercising it causes the Critical Illness Booster Benefit to cease. The plan also includes ICU benefits (including an additional Severe Intensive Care Unit Benefit for more severe ICU admissions) with a per-person cap of S$25,000. It further pays a lump-sum Death Benefit of S$5,000 if death occurs while the policy is in force.

extraction.document_summary: FWD Recover First is a critical illness insurance policy that combines multiple claim types rather than paying only from a fixed list once. The base component provides coverage for “37 late-stage critical illnesses” and pays 100% of the chosen sum insured “in one lump sum”; however, your policy “will be terminated once this base benefit is fully paid out.” A separate “Future Protect Benefit” supports early and intermediate critical illness (including impairment, surgery or ICU stay with invasive life support for at least 5 days) and provides a “Multiple payout via Reset Benefit” where the base sum insured resets 12 months after diagnosis, with future premiums waived upon a valid Future Protect claim. It also includes a “Special Benefit” paying S$25,000 per diagnosis for up to 6 claims (up to 10 named conditions), but it ends if you make a Future Protect claim. For certain critical illnesses, a 90-day waiting period from issuance/reinstatement applies; and exclusions include suicide/self-inflicted acts within one year and unlawful acts.
quality_notes: Brochure provides clear benefit names and key numbers (S$25,000 Special Benefit, 37 late-stage illnesses, S$5,000 Death Benefit, sum insured ranges, S$10,000 recovery programme value).

Some structural details (e.g., whether Future Protect Benefit and Recover First Benefit are strictly “base” vs rider components) are described in terms of “base benefit” and “rider” language is not consistently used; extracted fields are limited to what is explicitly stated.

extraction.document_summary: FWD Future First is a term life insurance plan designed to pay a lump sum if the person insured dies or is diagnosed with terminal illness, and it also includes an “Exclusive Recovery Programme” for eligible recovery-related expenses and support services. Under the base plan, on death the full sum insured is paid to beneficiaries, and FWD may pay S$5,000 in advance for funeral expenses upon request. If the person insured is diagnosed with terminal illness, the full sum insured is paid to you/beneficiaries. The base plan also includes up to 10 counselling/life coaching sessions (capped at S$5,000 total) and up to 3 legal advice sessions (capped at S$5,000 total). A spouse premium-free 2-year policy with a S$250,000 death sum insured is provided, subject to eligibility (spouse < 60).

extraction.document_summary: FWD Life Protection is a participating whole of life insurance policy that combines whole-life coverage with flexibility to draw income when you need it. It provides a boosted death cover via a “Life Protection Booster” where you can choose a multiplier factor of 2x, 3x, or 5x, and a minimum protection level (MPL) age option of 75 or 85; after the MPL age starts reducing, the boosted coverage is reduced by 10% annually for 5 years (so you maintain 50% of boosted coverage). For payouts, you can convert up to 80% of policy value (from as early as age 55) into annual income, with a customised payout term from as short as 10 years up to age 100, plus a guaranteed 10% additional booster on income payouts. Buyers should note that the brochure states certain conditions (e.g., pre-existing conditions) and exclusions may make benefits not payable, and that waiting periods may apply for certain benefits.
quality_notes: Brochure clearly names the base product (FWD Life Protection) and multiple add-on riders, and provides several explicit benefit mechanics (death payout basis, income conversion, retrenchment waiver).
Most numeric limits for CI riders are qualitative (number of conditions), while payout amounts for the early CI rider are specified (e.g., 20% of rider sum insured; max S$25,000).
Some important items are referenced but not fully detailed (e.g., underwriting/actual rider sum insured limits, waiting period specifics, full list of exclusions).

Supports retrenchment premium waiver (12 months if laid off and unemployed for at least 30 consecutive days before 65) and premium deferment up to 12 months (after meeting conditions). extraction.document_summary: This document is a marketing-only brochure for Great Eastern’s “Critical Cover Series” critical illness insurance. It positions the product as coverage that can pay again after a first critical illness claim (“continues over and over again, beyond your first claim”). The brochure explains the rationale: some critical illnesses can recur and increase the risk of a second or even a third critical illness, so the policy is meant to provide repeated protection. However, it does not state any specific list of covered critical illnesses, claim triggers, payout amounts, limits, waiting periods, renewal/coverage term mechanics, or underwriting requirements. It also states that the product has no savings or investment feature and there is no cash value if the policy ends or is terminated prematurely.

The only actionable product description is that it is critical illness coverage designed to pay repeatedly beyond the first claim.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s GREAT Life Advantage 4 is described as a whole-of-life, regular premium investment-linked (ILP) plan that aims to provide “lifetime protection against Death, Total and Permanent Disability and Terminal Illness.” The brochure also states that you can enhance coverage with “optional riders” that provide extra financial support for critical illness at “early, intermediate and critical stages,” but it does not provide rider names or specific payout amounts for these critical illness stages in the provided text. The plan includes a Child Cover Benefit that automatically covers your child(ren) and pays a S$20,000 payout for a “major life-impacting event.” Coverage chosen is guaranteed for the first 10 years. The policy offers flexibility to increase coverage at “eight life’s milestone events” without medical assessment, and allows single premium top-ups and withdrawals. Investment options include three GreatLink Dynamic Portfolios—Secure, Balanced, and Growth—with equity exposure ranges stated for each.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “GREAT Life Multiplier” is a life insurance solution used as the base for critical illness coverage via an optional “Critical Illness Multiplier Rider (E&I)” (early & intermediate stage and critical stage). The rider uses a multiplier to scale the insured critical illness benefit, with examples shown: for Lola, the early/intermediate portion is “S$30,000 (multiplied 5 times to S$150,000 until age 75)” and the critical-stage portion is “S$50,000 (multiplied 5 times to S$250,000 until age 75)”; for Mike, the same structure is “S$30,000 (multiplied 10 times to S$300,000 until age 65)” and “S$50,000 (multiplied 10 times to S$500,000 until age 65).” A “Parent Care Rider” provides age-related-condition coverage without medical assessment for parents (example mentions Severe Dementia/Alzheimer’s), and a “Payer Benefit Enhanced (CI) Rider” waives future premiums upon a critical illness diagnosis (as stated). The brochure also mentions “Special Benefits” under the CI Multiplier Rider (E&I) paying “25% of the rider sum assured” (up to six claims).

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s GREAT Term 2 is a regular premium, non-participating term insurance plan that provides coverage for death and terminal illness. extraction.document_summary: GREAT Hospital Cash is a standalone health insurance plan that pays cash benefits when the Life Assured is hospitalised for illness or injury, and when additional intensive care, post-surgery, or (for some plans) day surgery events occur. The core cash mechanic is: if hospitalisation lasts for 12 consecutive hours or longer (or involves room-and-board charges), you receive a Daily Hospital Cash Benefit. The daily amount depends on the plan tier: Plan A pays S$100/day, Plan B S$200/day, Plan C S$400/day, and Plan D S$600/day, with coverage “up to 730 days per Hospitalisation”. If the Life Assured is in ICU, an extra Daily Hospital Cash Benefit applies up to 60 days (“Additional Daily Hospital Cash Benefit - Intensive Care Unit”). The plan also includes a Get Well Benefit: hospitalisation lump sum of up to S$1,800 per hospitalisation (at least 3 days of room-and-board charges), plus a separate post-surgery lump sum (excluding day surgery) up to S$1,800. It further provides Emergency Accidental Outpatient reimbursement of up to S$100/200/400/600 per period of insurance, but treatment must be given within 72 hours of the accident.

policies.quick_summary: GREAT Hospital Cash pays cash for hospitalisation after a minimum qualifying period (12 hours or room & board charges), with higher payouts for ICU and additional lump sums for qualifying hospitalisation and surgery-related events. It also reimburses certain emergency outpatient treatment following an accident. The plan is offered in four tiers (Plan A–D), with Daily Hospital Cash Benefit ranging from S$100/day to S$600/day and Get Well Benefit amounts up to S$1,800 per hospitalisation (subject to the stated conditions and limits). Day surgery has separate (lower) lump sum amounts. ICU cash is capped at 60 days per hospitalisation.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s LifeSecure is a disability insurance product that pays a regular monthly benefit for total and permanent disability or for inability to perform at least 2 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). The monthly payout is stated as “up to S$5,000” for up to a lifetime, and it is intended to help cover disability-related care at home or in hospital and related aids/equipment and home modifications. For stand-alone LifeSecure, a lump sum death benefit equal to 3 times the monthly benefit applies if the life insured dies during the coverage term. A separate “payback benefit” is payable after a deferment period (90 days or 180 days), and then pays a lump sum of 3 times or 6 times the monthly benefit insured. The brochure also describes an out-of-school disability benefit for a child aged 7–16, adding S$500 per month on top of the insured child monthly benefit (ending at age 16, with at least 12 monthly installments).
quality_notes: Document gives the core benefit mechanics, but does not clearly state the full set of plan options (e.g., how the monthly benefit is selected beyond examples).

Premium tables are provided for illustrative S$1,000 monthly benefit (stand-alone) and S$500 monthly benefit (as a rider), but eligibility/age limits for the adult coverage are not explicitly enumerated beyond footnotes.

Can be purchased stand-alone or as a rider attached to selected whole life plans offered by Great Eastern (as stated). Monthly benefit shown as up to S$5,000 for up to a lifetime; payback lump sum after a deferment period (3x or 6x the monthly benefit). No cash value/investment feature stated.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s “Maternity Protect Series” (illustrated with “Maternity Protect Multiplier”) is a health/maternity protection plan for pregnancy, childbirth, and early childhood up to around the child’s toddler years (up to 3 years old). It provides a fixed “Pregnancy & Childbirth Complication Beneﬁt (Mother)” and “Hospital Care Beneﬁt” for both mother and child, with additional supports for eligible developmental delays and psychological consultations (including per-session limits). The brochure also highlights an “Early Delivery by Caesarean Section” benefit (up to S$3,750* as an additional payout) and “Mum Again” support described as a “Parental Retrenchment Cash Beneﬁt” payable once up to S$5,000 if either parent is retrenched unexpectedly. A key caveat is that the “GREAT Life Multiplier” is described as a separate policy, and other add-on/transfer options rely on timing rules such as exercising within 100 days from birth without medical underwriting (for eligible options).

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s “PayAssure” is a stand-alone disability income insurance plan that pays a monthly benefit during the benefit period if you are not engaged in any gainful occupation due to disability. After the chosen pre-beneﬁt period of 60, 90, or 180 days, you receive monthly benefits for as long as you continue to suffer from disability, up to age 55, 60, or 65 (depending on the plan option) or your death. Premiums due while you are receiving the monthly benefit are waived, but premiums falling due during the pre-beneﬁt period must be paid in full. If your present earnings are 85% or less of pre-disability earnings, partial monthly benefits may apply. The plan can also reimburse rehabilitation expenses (certified as necessary) up to three times the selected monthly benefit, and provides a death benefit of six times the selected monthly benefit.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern DIRECT – GREAT Term is a Direct Purchase Insurance term life plan providing protection for Death, Terminal Illness, and Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) for a fixed coverage period. You can choose either (1) DIRECT – GREAT Term: a 20-year term plan or coverage until age 65, or (2) DIRECT – GREAT 5yr Term: a five-year term that is renewable for the same sum assured up to age 80, with each renewal period lasting five years. Premiums are guaranteed and the premium payment term follows the chosen policy term. The plan itself has no savings/investment features. The brochure also allows attaching a DIRECT – GREAT Critical Care rider (or 5yr Critical Care rider), which accelerates the rider’s basic sum assured upon diagnosis of specified critical illnesses, with a separate maximum CI benefit cap of S$3,000,000 across all policies/riders. TPD is capped at S$5,000,000 across all policies/riders issued by the Company on the same life assured.
quality_notes: The document is mostly feature-level text; payout amounts for base Death/Terminal Illness/TPD are not explicitly stated (except for TPD cap and CI rider mechanics).
No underwriting, medical exam, free-look, grace period, or exact definition of benefit payment for Death/Terminal Illness is provided beyond definitions.
Some structured formatting is missing (e.g., no clear tables of plan benefits/premiums), limiting extraction to what is explicitly described.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “DIRECT – GREAT Life II” is a Direct Purchase whole life plan designed to provide lifetime protection against Death, Terminal Illness and Total & Permanent Disability (TPD), while accumulating cash value over time. It is “easy to understand” and can be bought directly with no financial advisory cost (subject to direct purchase availability). Premium payment can be chosen up to age 70 next birthday or up to age 85 next birthday (document states all ages are age next birthday). The base TPD benefit is limited to a maximum TPD Benefit of S$5,000,000 across all policies and riders on the same life, and is only applicable if TPD occurs before the policy anniversary when the life assured is age 65 next birthday. There is also a Direct – Great Critical Care 70/85 rider option providing accelerated payouts for 30 critical illnesses, with an overall CI benefit cap of S$3,000,000.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern Cares Term Plan is an affordable term life insurance product focused on providing basic protection for death and terminal illness. The brochure states it is offered exclusively through selected charities and non-profit organisations, and is designed to help dependants with financial support in the event of the life assured’s demise. Cover can be chosen from S$100,000 to S$300,000, and policy terms are selectable either “up to age 85” or “up to age 100”. The plan pays a lump sum for covered events; for example, a S$200,000 coverage with a policy term up to age 100 pays S$200,000 as a lump sum if death occurs (illustration). It is stated to have no savings/investment feature, so there is no cash value if terminated early.
quality_notes: The brochure provides high-level product features (coverage range, term up to age 85/100, lump-sum payout) but does not include detailed underwriting rules, exact benefit definitions for terminal illness, exclusions list, grace period, or free-look period.
Some figures are presented as marketing/illustration (e.g., “S$120 a year” and the example premium/payout) without confirming guaranteed limits or full rate tables.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern’s GREAT Life Advantage 4 is a whole-of-life, regular-premium investment-linked (ILP) plan that provides lifetime protection against Death, Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) and Terminal Illness. The brochure states “guaranteed protection for the first 10 years,” meaning the chosen cover is provided for the first 10 years of the policy. Coverage can be increased at eight “life’s milestone events” without medical assessment. It also allows single premium top-ups and “withdrawals whenever needed.” The plan includes an automatic Child Cover Benefit for any future children, with a stated payout of S$20,000 for a “major life-impacting event.” Investment is via GreatLink Dynamic Portfolios (Secure, Balanced, Growth), with stated equity/fixed-income exposure ranges.

extraction.document_summary: GREAT Life Multiplier (Great Eastern) is a life insurance solution designed to provide protection while addressing both your own needs and your family’s. The brochure describes a base “Death Benefit under GREAT Life Multiplier”, and it is commonly enhanced with optional riders: (1) Critical Illness Multiplier Rider (E&I) for early/intermediate and critical stage critical illnesses, and (2) Parent Care Rider for guaranteed coverage for age-related conditions (e.g., Severe Dementia/Alzheimer’s Disease) “without medical assessment” at the point of coverage. A further feature mentioned is “Beneficiary access” (subject to nomination rules) for future decisions. The document also states that each “Special Benefit, Juvenile Benefit or Senior Benefit provides a payout equivalent to 25% of the rider sum assured” and that up to six claims can be made for different covered events. A key limitation explicitly stated is that pre-existing conditions are excluded.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern GREAT Term 2 is a regular premium, non-participating term life plan designed to provide coverage for death and terminal illness with level premiums throughout the policy term. The document states it is available with add-on critical illness options, including “Complete Living Care Rider 2”, which covers critical illness across early, intermediate, and late stages; it also states a “late stage critical illness rider” option for those who want only later-stage coverage. For early or intermediate stage critical illness under the named rider arrangement, the brochure specifies an accelerated lump-sum payout of up to S$350,000 per claim (subject to the rider’s sum assured). A key flexibility feature is the Conversion Privilege: it can be exercised once (full or partial), with conversion not later than the policy anniversary when the life assured’s next birthday is 70, and without further health assessments—provided the new policy’s basic sum assured does not exceed GREAT Term 2’s basic sum assured. The policy also references options for TPD and accident riders and premium waiver riders (details not fully shown).

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern Prestige Life Gold (SGD/USD) is a single-premium life insurance design intended to provide lifetime protection and a legacy. It is described as a “participating whole of life insurance plan” together with a “non-participating term rider that covers both death and terminal illness.” The key value mechanic is a “Multiplier” of the basic sum assured, stated as up to 3.15 times for the SGD plan and up to 3.45 times for the USD plan, with the multiplier expiring at age 85 next birthday unless extended to age 100 via the Multiplier Extender option (with conditions such as no previously approved claims and no current claim applications). The brochure also states a minimum cash surrender value of at least 80% of the single premium from day 1, and notes foreign exchange exposure if USD is not the home currency.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “GREAT Golden Protector” is a personal accident insurance product focused on accidents occurring on public transportation or in a private car. It highlights a payout of “up to 300%” and specifies “Receive 3 times the payout upon Accidental Death or Permanent Disablement caused by an accident on public transportation or a private car”. For hospitalisation, it provides “a cash benefit of up to S$200 per day,” and it also states that this hospital cash “covers hospital stays due to Dengue Fever or other Infectious Diseases.” The brochure also mentions a discount feature—“25% off premiums on 2nd life assured”—for Singapore Citizens/PRs when adding a spouse as the 2nd life assured via a financial representative, but this is not the core coverage mechanism.

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “GREAT Junior Protector” is a Singapore personal accident insurance plan for children (premiums quoted per day). The brochure highlights a daily hospital cash benefit of up to S$150 per day for hospitalisation due to an accident or for specified Infectious Diseases. It also states that the plan provides up to 3 times the payout for Accidental Death or Permanent Disablement. The Infectious Disease benefit applies from as young as 15 days after birth or 15 days after discharge from hospital, whichever is later, and the daily benefit is linked to the annual premiums of Plan A, Plan B or Plan C divided by 365 (GST included, subject to change). A key limitation stated is that Infectious Disease excludes HIV and STD-related diseases, and the policy is only for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs).

extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “GREAT Protector Active” is a personal accident plan offering “personal accident coverage of up to S$4.5 million” for “total and permanent disability, or loss of use of limbs or sight due to an accident.” The document describes a lump-sum disability payout and also a “Benefit Booster” feature that can increase the payout by “up to 150%” for certain accident scenarios (e.g., when the Life Assured is a pedestrian/cyclist/passenger in road accidents or on public conveyance as a passenger), with exclusions such as “PMDs do not qualify.” The product offers plan options by sum assured: Basic (S$200,000), Classic (S$500,000), and Elite (S$1,000,000), with correspondingly higher “Disability” amounts listed in the table. Optional add-ons include the Lifestyle Rider (reimbursements for TCM up to S$1,000 per accident; scar removal up to S$1,000 per accident; dental up to S$700 per lifetime) and the Recovery Cash Rider (weekly income up to S$200, up to 104 weeks per accident). A key limitation noted is eligibility for “increased-risk activities” and the insurer’s “absolute discretion” on eligibility.
quality_notes: The document text has missing/blank product name placeholders near the illustration (likely plan/rider names removed during conversion), but the overall product name is identifiable from the file name and the content.

The table headings for some disability payout sub-benefits (labelled B and C) are not explicitly explained in the extracted text; amounts are present but benefit meaning is only partially supported by narrative.
No underwriting, waiting/free-look days, renewal, or comprehensive exclusion list is explicitly provided.

Plans (Basic/Classic/Elite) are shown by disability sum assured options (S$200,000 / S$500,000 / S$1,000,000). extraction.document_summary: This document excerpt appears to relate to Great Eastern’s Personal Accident Insurance product “PA Supreme”, but the core brochure content (policy definition, benefits table with limits, and key terms) is largely missing. The visible section includes a “Table of Benefit / Summary of Benefits” listing areas that may be covered “up to the benefit limit as specified”: medical expenses, physician’s expenses (noted as up to the benefit limit with “S$50 excess”), mobility aid, personal belongings, and evacuation & repatriation. extraction.document_summary: Great Eastern “Prestige PACare” is a personal accident plan providing worldwide accident protection with 24/7 emergency assistance. The core benefit is Accidental Death & Permanent Disablement, with coverage of S$1 million to S$3.5 million (sum assured) for death or permanent disablement due to an accident, stated as “high 24/7 worldwide coverage of up to S$3.5 million.” An optional feature supplements the plan with Medical Expense Reimbursement up to S$20,000 for each accident, including Complementary Medicine Practitioner treatment up to S$500 and Mobility Aids up to S$1,000. The plan also provides emergency assistance services covering medical evacuation/repatriation and related assistance. Benefits are reduced by 50% for “high-risk activities,” and terrorism benefits are limited to S$2 million per life assured across this plan and all similar plans/riders. The policy is guaranteed renewable annually until age 75, with a 5% renewal discount from the 2nd policy year (regardless of claims).

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Accident Care and Singlife Family Accident Care are Singapore Life Ltd yearly renewable personal accident insurance plans with worldwide coverage for accidental death or injury. The core benefit is Accidental Death and Dismemberment (ADDB) with coverage options (Singlife Accident Care: S$250,000 to S$3,000,000; Singlife Family Accident Care: S$500,000 or S$1,000,000) and multipliers: up to 150% for the base ADDB schedule and “3 times”/“2 times” payout scenarios depending on where the accident occurred. They also include daily cash hospital income (up to 365 days per accident) and additional benefits such as Annual Leave Compensation (S$100/day) and a Life Stage Event lump sum for accidental death/TPI occurring 12 months from named life events. Key limitation: benefits are only payable upon an accident occurring, and Singlife Accident Care has no savings/cash value.
quality_notes: Document clearly distinguishes Singlife Accident Care vs Singlife Family Accident Care and provides multiple plan tiers and numeric benefit limits.
Exclusions are not comprehensively listed; only one explicitly excluded scenario is stated (“Workplaces… not covered”).

extraction.document_summary: This brochure from Singlife describes two independently marketed personal accident insurance products with worldwide coverage: Singlife Accident Care (individual cover) and Singlife Family Accident Care (shared family cover). Both are annual renewable plans with accidental death and dismemberment as the core benefit, paying percentage-based amounts tied to the Accidental Death and Dismemberment Benefit (ADDB) schedule, with higher payouts in specified travel/transport/fire scenarios. Base plans also provide cash benefits for hospitalisation (daily cash for up to 365 days per accident), plus services and family-related event/leave compensation options, including a Life Stage Event lump sum paid if the accident occurs within 12 months. For expanded protection, the brochure adds named riders (Accident Reimbursement Cover II, Accidental Fracture Cover III, Weekly Income Cover II) with multiple Plan 1–4 tiers and per-accident/per-policy-year limits.
quality_notes: Includes extensive numeric benefit tables for base plans and rider plan tiers.
Exclusions are referenced generally (“definitions and exclusions”) but no specific excluded events/circumstances are explicitly enumerated in the provided text.
Entry/eligibility details (e.g., occupation class, minimum/maximum entry ages) are only partially stated; many underwriting fields are not explicitly provided.

policies.quick_summary: Annual renewable personal accident insurance with worldwide coverage for accidental death and dismemberment, daily hospitalisation income, and other cash/services benefits; offers Lite/Standard/Plus/Prestige/Pinnacle tiers. Optional riders add medical reimbursement, fracture/dislocation with physiotherapy support, and weekly income for temporary disability (accident and sickness). Rider tier limits are stated per accident and/or per policy year with Plan 1–4 options for each rider category included in the brochure table set-up for this base product (not Family). The brochure states the product has no savings/investment feature and therefore no cash value.

policies.quick_summary: Annual renewable personal accident insurance with worldwide coverage for accidental death and dismemberment, daily hospitalisation cash income, and other cash benefits, designed for families with shared payout limits. It covers a minimum of two and up to six lives under one policy, with one shared Accidental Death and Dismemberment limit across all Lives Assured (claims paid as they come up until the shared limit is reached). Optional riders add medical reimbursement, fracture/dislocation with physiotherapy, and weekly income for temporary disability, with a separate (Family) rider variant in the brochure tables.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Multipay Critical Illness II is a multipayout critical illness insurance plan covering 135 critical illness conditions across early, intermediate and severe stages, with continued protection through multiple payouts (including recurrence). It pays: (1) 100% of sum assured for one eligible early/intermediate condition in one lump sum; (2) 100% of sum assured for severe stage conditions (one claim per CI Group), with a stated overall Critical Illness Benefit cap of 600% of sum assured; (3) recurrent payouts after the Critical Illness Benefit has ceased—150% of sum assured per eligible recurrent claim (up to 2 claims, 300% total). A first severe-stage diagnosis also triggers premium waiver. Additional “special benefits” can add 20% of sum assured per eligible item/condition with a cap of S$25,000 (or equivalent currency) per life, and an Advance Care Option can add another 75% of sum assured (and terminates the Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit). Coverage term is selectable from 10 years up to age 99 (in one-year intervals) and can be taken in SGD, USD, GBP, EUR, AUD or HKD. The brochure also states there is no savings/investment feature, hence no cash value if the policy ends.
quality_notes: Brochure contains clear benefit mechanics, payout percentages, caps, waiting periods, and recurrence claim limits.
Detailed lists of covered conditions are referenced but not provided; the brochure points to the Product Summary for full lists.
Underwriting details, precise premium payment term, and free-look/grace period are not stated in this extract.
Some benefit sub-clauses are embedded as “Important Notes” and give necessary constraints (e.g., ICU in Singapore admission, claim counts, benefit cessation triggers).
