Premiums are waived upon the first severe stage diagnosis, and additional “special benefits” can pay extra 20% of sum assured (capped at S$25,000 per life). An Advance Care Option can add an extra 75% of sum assured and terminates the recurrent component. Coverage term selectable from 10 years to age 99 and currency choices include SGD, USD, GBP, EUR, AUD, HKD.

extraction.document_summary: This brochure describes two Singlife “Supplements” that are designed to boost national long-term care payouts under CareShield Life (CSHL) or ElderShield (ESH). It covers Singlife CareShield Standard and Singlife CareShield Plus. Both provide additional monthly severe disability payouts on top of the underlying government scheme payout (Standard: for inability to perform at least three ADLs; Plus: for inability to perform at least two ADLs). The supplement monthly payout is stated to be S$200 to S$5,000 more each month, with the payout either fixed or increasing (2% or 3% annually). It also adds other components such as an additional monthly “Add-on Benefit” for up to 12 months (triggered by inability to perform 2 ADLs/1 ADL for Standard/Plus), potential lump-sum and death/rehabilitation-related amounts (described as multiple of monthly benefit), plus waiver reliefs for mild disability and MediSave premium payment support.
quality_notes: Document clearly distinguishes Singlife CareShield Standard vs Singlife CareShield Plus by ADL thresholds and provides multiple payout mechanics and time limits.

Some quantitative features (e.g., exact benefit multiples/amount definitions for certain benefits) are stated, but other details are deferred to the referenced Product Summary and are therefore not extracted here.
The brochure uses footnotes and examples; only explicitly stated facts are extracted into structured fields.

policies.quick_summary: A CareShield Life/ElderShield supplement that adds severe disability monthly payouts on top of the government scheme. For Standard, payouts start when the Life Assured cannot perform at least three ADLs, and the extra monthly benefit is stated as S$200 to S$5,000. It can be fixed or increasing (2% or 3% annually). It also includes an Add-on Benefit (up to 12 months) and waiver reliefs for mild disability, with a 90-day deferment period for selected benefits and MediSave premium payment support (up to S$600 per calendar year). Note: Some benefit details are subject to the Product Summary and the Deferment Period.

extraction.document_summary: This brochure describes two Singlife government-approved CareShield Life/ElderShield “supplement” plans: Singlife CareShield Standard and Singlife CareShield Plus. Both pay an additional monthly benefit on top of the national CareShield Life/ElderShield severe disability payout when the Life Assured meets the plans’ severe disability definition (based on inability to perform Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)). Singlife CareShield Standard requires inability to perform at least three ADLs, while CareShield Plus requires inability to perform at least two ADLs. The brochure also adds benefits beyond the base severe disability monthly payout: a monthly Add-on benefit for up to 12 months (with earlier ADL triggers for Plus vs Standard), Dependant Care Benefit up to 36 months, Caregiver Relief Benefit up to 12 months, and lump-sum payouts (including a death lump sum that is three times the last monthly benefit). Payment mode flexibility includes limited premium payment options and MediSave usage (up to S$600 per calendar year). A key caveat is the 90-day deferment period before specified benefits are paid.
quality_notes: Document clearly differentiates Singlife CareShield Standard vs Singlife CareShield Plus and states their ADL-based severe disability triggers.

Exact dollar amounts are given as ranges for the additional monthly benefit (S$200 to S$5,000 more each month), but other benefit components (e.g., exact percentages) are given in “Important notes” rather than a table; these were still extracted as written.
Entry age, maximum coverage age, and exact premium amounts/limits are not stated in the brochure.
No explicit exclusions section is provided; only procedural caveats (e.g., deferment period, MediSave limit) are stated.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Comprehensive Critical Illness II is a single-payout critical illness plan that pays a one-time lump sum when you are diagnosed with any of the 135 covered critical illness conditions across early, intermediate and severe stages. The core payout is 100% of your Sum Assured. The brochure also provides add-on payouts that can increase total benefits depending on the event: (1) a further additional 20% of Sum Assured for surgical removal of a Benign Tumour (suspected malignancy) or diagnosis of a Borderline Malignant Tumour, capped at S$25,000; (2) if you spend 4 days or more in the ICU in one hospital admission, you receive an additional 20% of Sum Assured, capped at S$25,000; and (3) a Special Benefit for 27 conditions pays an additional 20% of Sum Assured up to S$25,000 per life per condition, with a maximum of six claims. It also states a death payout of S$5,000 during the coverage period. Key buyer caveats include claim limits (e.g., only one claim under certain benefits, and the Special Benefit has a per-condition and total-claim maximum) and that waiting period and survival period are applicable.
quality_notes: Main benefits and caps are stated clearly (100% Sum Assured, additional 20% with S$25,000 caps, and death payout of S$5,000).
Eligibility ages (entry age range) are not explicitly stated; only benefit cessation ages and coverage-period choices are described.
Underwriting level, medical exam requirement, free-look/grace period, and exclusions are not explicitly provided in the brochure text supplied.

policies.quick_summary: Single-payout critical illness plan: pays 100% of Sum Assured as a lump sum on diagnosis of 135 covered critical illnesses (across early/intermediate/severe stages). Additional benefits may pay extra 20% of Sum Assured for specified events (benign/borderline tumours, ICU stay ≥4 days, and a Special Benefit for 27 conditions), each subject to caps and claim limits. Death during coverage period pays S$5,000. Coverage period can be chosen from 10 years up to age 99 (in 1-year intervals) and payout limits can be converted if not in SGD. Waiting and survival periods are stated as applicable for certain benefits.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Essential Critical Illness II is a multi-protection critical illness plan that pays a lump-sum upon diagnosis of a covered Critical Illness, Total and Permanent Disability, Terminal Illness, or Death. It is designed to cover people with specified pre-existing conditions, including Type 2 Diabetes, pre-diabetes and/or “the 3 Highs” (high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and high BMI). Applicants complete “just 6 questions” with “no medical check-up needed” if no further medical underwriting is required. Benefit payouts include: (1) standard lump-sum payment tied to the Death Benefit Sum Assured for covered events; (2) a diabetes-related extra lump sum of 20% of the Death Benefit Sum Assured (up to S$25,000 per condition per life); and (3) an extra lump sum for “Angioplasty & Other Invasive Treatment For Coronary Artery” of 10% of Sum Assured (up to S$25,000) that reduces the Sum Assured by the same amount. It also has a no-claims reward of 20% of total premiums paid at the end of the policy term.
quality_notes: Brochure provides clear payout mechanics for the diabetes-related extra payout, angioplasty payout, and no-claims reward.
Some key product underwriting/administration fields (e.g., entry ages, free-look period, full list of TPD/terminal definitions) are not included in the provided text.
No explicit exclusions are stated in the provided excerpt; only limitation/caveat notes are provided.

policies.quick_summary: Multi-protection critical illness plan with lump-sum payouts for covered critical illnesses, TPD, terminal illness and death, with special add-ons for diabetic conditions (extra 20% up to S$25,000/condition) and a separate angioplasty payout (10% up to S$25,000, reducing sum assured by the same amount). Includes a no-claims reward of 20% of total premiums paid at end of term; designed to cover certain pre-existing conditions with a 6-question application (no medical check-up needed if no further underwriting required). Even if a payout has already occurred, the death-related mechanics and diabetic extra benefit rules specify how remaining amounts are determined.

important_caveats: No medical examination is required if the applicant’s responses to the 6 health questions indicate no further medical underwriting is required.

Death benefit payout depends on whether there has been a prior claim: either 100% of the Sum Assured or total premiums paid (whichever is higher) for no prior claims; for prior claims, the calculation is adjusted and excludes Diabetic Conditions Beneﬁt in the stated manner.

Diabetic Conditions Beneﬁt pays an additional 20% of the Death Benefit Sum Assured up to S$25,000 per condition per life and ceases once that additional portion is fully paid or when the policy terminates (whichever earlier). Only one claim can be made on the same Diabetic Condition.

Angioplasty & Other Invasive Treatment For Coronary Artery pays 10% of Sum Assured (subject to maximum claimable limit of S$25,000) and reduces the Sum Assured by the same amount; only once and payable as an early payout of the Death Beneﬁt. Other benefits continue based on the prevailing Sum Assured after that payment.
If there are no savings/investment features, there is no cash value if the policy ends or is terminated prematurely.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Multipay Critical Illness II is a critical illness policy with multiple payouts across early, intermediate and severe stages, plus additional “extra cushioning” benefits and a death benefit. Under the Critical Illness Benefit, the first early/intermediate diagnosis pays 100% of sum assured per eligible claim (up to 2 claims total and subject to CI limits), while the first severe stage diagnosis pays 150% of sum assured, with a maximum total payout of 600% of sum assured under this benefit. Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit then allows further payouts of 150% per eligible recurrent claim, up to 2 claims (maximum total 300% of sum assured). On a first severe stage diagnosis, premiums are waived and the Advance Care Option can convert the Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit into an extra lump sum equal to 75% of sum assured (and the recurrent benefit terminates). Coverage term is chosen up to age 99 (in one-year intervals) and may be in SGD, USD, GBP, EUR, AUD or HKD.
quality_notes: Core benefit structure (early/intermediate/severe, recurrent, advance care option, extra benefits, death benefit) and key payout caps are stated.
Exact eligibility age limits, underwriting method, and any medical examination requirement are not provided in the brochure.

Full lists of covered conditions are referenced but not included in the document; only counts (e.g., 135 conditions; 34 “Special Benefit” conditions; 6 severe and 60 severe recurrence groups) are given.

policies.quick_summary: Multipay critical illness plan with up to 600% sum assured under the Critical Illness Benefit (early/intermediate/severe stage) and an additional Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit up to 300% (up to 2 recurrent claims). A first severe stage diagnosis triggers premium waiver and may be converted via the Advance Care Option into an extra 75% lump sum, terminating the recurrent benefit. Also provides extra 20% per life for ICU stay of 4+ days, and extra 20% per life per condition for 34 Special Benefit conditions (with a total of up to six claims under that Special Benefit). Includes a S$5,000 death benefit during coverage.
coverage_scope: Critical Illness Benefit covering early, intermediate and severe stage critical illnesses (135 conditions referenced)
Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit for certain specified severe stage conditions and recurrences
Advance Care Option convertible from first severe stage diagnosis to an extra payout and termination of recurrent benefit
Intensive Care Unit (ICU) stay extra benefit (4 days or more) for confirmed necessary medical treatment
Special Benefit extra payout for certain specified conditions (34 conditions referenced)
Death benefit of S$5,000 during coverage period
policies.coverage_term_description: Choice of coverage term from 10 years up to age 99 (in one-year intervals).
policy_termination_events: Critical Illness Benefit ceases once 600% of the Sum Assured is fully paid out
Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit ceases once 300% of the Sum Assured is fully paid out or when the Advance Care Option is successfully exercised, whichever is earlier
Certain extra benefits cease on policy anniversary at age 85 (or earlier upon claim or policy expiry), as described for each extra benefit
important_caveats: Recurrent benefit is terminated when the Advance Care Option is exercised.
Recurrent benefit only applies after the Critical Illness Benefit has ceased, and is subject to waiting/survival period requirements (full details referenced to Product Summary).
The ICU stay benefit requires the ICU stay of 4 days or more (due to illness or accident) to be in one hospital admission in Singapore and confirmed as Necessary Medical Treatment.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Multipay Critical Illness II is a critical illness insurance plan that provides multiple payouts across early, intermediate, and severe stage critical illnesses. It covers “135 conditions” with continued protection after diagnosis, including recurrence. Under the Critical Illness Benefit, an early/intermediate stage diagnosis pays 100% of your sum assured per eligible claim (up to 2 claims and up to 300% total under the Recurrent Illness Benefit section’s limits described), while specified severe stage diagnoses pay 100% of sum assured and can be repeated within defined group rules, subject to a total cap. The plan can reach a maximum total payout of “900% of the Sum Assured.” Upon your first severe stage diagnosis, premiums are waived and an Advance Care Option may be exercised to receive an additional “75% of the Sum Assured” in one lump sum; this option ends the Recurrent Critical Illness Benefit. A separate death benefit of S$5,000 applies if death occurs during the coverage period. Coverage terms can be chosen “from 10 years up to age 99 (in one-year intervals)” and benefits can be paid in SGD, USD, GBP, EUR, AUD or HKD.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife CareShield Standard and Singlife CareShield Plus are government-approved CareShield Life/ElderShield supplement plans by Singlife (Singapore Life Ltd. underwrites). They pay additional support for severe disability on top of the national schemes’ severe disability payouts. The key difference is the disability trigger: Standard pays when you cannot perform at least three of six ADLs, while Plus requires at least two ADLs and can be set to increasing payouts (2% or 3% annually for Plus, versus fixed for Standard). Both plans include extra monthlies beyond the base severe-disability monthly payout (Add-on Benefit for up to 12 months), and provide lump-sum relief when severe disability occurs, plus family-oriented benefits tied to a child below age 22 and caregiver relief. A 90-day deferment period applies to selected benefits, and MediSave usage is limited to S$600 per calendar year per life assured.
quality_notes: Document clearly distinguishes Singlife CareShield Standard vs Singlife CareShield Plus and states key ADL thresholds, payout structures, and several benefit types.
No specific entry-age ranges, coverage duration end ages, or detailed underwriting rules are stated in the provided text.
Exact premium amounts are not provided; only payment-period options and MediSave limits are stated.

policies.quick_summary: CareShield Life/ElderShield supplement that pays additional monthly benefits for severe disability (unable to perform at least 3 of 6 ADLs), with a fixed payout option, plus add-on, lump-sum, and family/caregiver benefits. A 90-day deferment period applies to selected benefits, and MediSave use is capped at S$600 per calendar year per life assured. Premiums may be payable up to a specified time (including up to age 98) or for a limited period (with limited-time options described). Additional increases of monthly benefit may be possible without underwriting hassle but are limited to 50% of initial monthly benefit.

policies.premium_payment_term_description: You can choose a premium payment period: pay up to the policy anniversary after you turn 98, or pay for a limited time. For limited time, the brochure states two ways: (a) pay up to the policy anniversary after they turn 68, or (b) pay for 20 years from entry age if joining at age 49 or older (the later of the two applies).
important_caveats: Severe disability definition differs by plan: for Standard it requires inability to perform at least three of the six ADLs.

The brochure states a 90-day Deferment Period from confirmation/certification by an Appointed Assessor as severely disabled; monthly benefit, Lump Sum Benefit, Dependant Care Benefit and Caregiver Relief Benefit are paid after the Deferment Period.
Waiver of Premium is applicable after the Deferment Period.
MediSave can be used up to S$600 per calendar year per life assured; premiums exceeding this limit must be paid in cash.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Dementia Cover is a long-term care protection plan focused on cognitive decline, with added mental health and certain injury-related support after a dementia diagnosis. It provides annual payouts of up to S$10,000 for cognitive decline/mental health, with “late dementia” Cognitive Care paid over 10 years up to age 99 (the brochure states late-dementia coverage lasts 10 years from diagnosis and the policy terminates after the full Cognitive Care payout). It also includes the Mental Care Benefit for major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and early/intermediate dementia, paid up to S$50,000 over 5 years. There are also one-time lump-sum payouts up to S$10,000 each for Emotional Resilience (depressive or anxiety disorder) and Medical Expense (accidental burns or fractures). The brochure notes the policy is standalone and not MediSave-approved, and mentions “All age mentioned are Age Next Birthday.”
quality_notes: Brochure clearly states key benefit structures and caps (e.g., up to S$10,000 annual; up to S$50,000 over 5 years; one-time up to S$10,000).
Entry age, premium frequency, underwriting, and renewal/termination conditions beyond the Cognitive Care payout end are not stated in a contract-like way.
No discrete plan tiers (e.g., Plan A/B/C) are named; only a selectable “benefit amount” range (S$200 to S$2,000) is provided.

extraction.document_summary: This brochure describes two government-approved ElderShield-enhancement supplements from Singlife: Singlife ElderShield Standard and Singlife ElderShield Plus. Both boost your monthly Severe Disability benefit and pay it monthly for up to 12 years or for life, as long as you remain severely disabled (unable to perform a defined number of ADLs). Standard requires inability to perform at least 3 of 6 ADLs, while Plus requires at least 2 of 6. The payout level is stated as S$600 to S$5,000 monthly, plus a Dependant Care Benefit of S$200 monthly for up to 36 months if you have a child aged 22 and below at claim. Both supplements also include a lump-sum for severe disability (up to three times the first monthly benefit) and a death payout of three times the last monthly benefit if death occurs while receiving monthly/Rehabilitation payouts. Premiums can be paid via MediSave (up to S$600 per calendar year). Premiums are waived while receiving the Severe Disability or Rehabilitation benefits. Standard additionally includes a Rehabilitation Benefit if you recover but are still unable to perform 2 ADLs and need physical assistance throughout, and Standard also notes a premium payment term limited to up to policy anniversary or to age 65 (ANB-based).
quality_notes: Document clearly separates benefits/features for ElderShield Standard vs ElderShield Plus, including ADL threshold differences.
Some eligibility/term details are referenced as footnotes (e.g., “up to 12 years or for life”), but the brochure states the key mechanics in the main sections.
Quantitative plan options (e.g., S$300/S$400 ElderShield basic scheme) are mentioned for context, but no standalone new-customer premium/age limits for the Singlife supplements are explicitly given.

Several important clauses are in “Important notes” but are not expressed with complete legal precision (e.g., MediSave cap, premium payment term constraint), so values are extracted only where explicitly stated.

policies.quick_summary: Singlife ElderShield Standard is a Singlife ElderShield supplement that enhances the government ElderShield scheme by paying an additional monthly benefit for severe disability (S$600 to S$5,000 monthly) for up to 12 years or for life, when you are severely disabled and unable to perform at least 3 of 6 ADLs. It can also pay a lump-sum for severe disability (up to three times the first monthly benefit) and a death payout equal to three times the last monthly benefit if death occurs while receiving benefits. Standard includes a Rehabilitation Benefit after recovery from severe disability—if you are still unable to perform 2 ADLs (even with special aids) and need physical assistance—payable for the remaining benefit payout duration. A Dependant Care Benefit adds S$200 monthly for up to 36 months for eligible children. Premiums can be paid using MediSave (up to S$600 per calendar year) and are waived while receiving the Severe Disability or Rehabilitation benefits.

extraction.document_summary: This brochure describes Singlife Direct Purchase Insurance (DPI) life insurance that can be bought directly without a financial adviser. It offers two main base products: DIRECT – Singlife Term Life (fixed-period protection) and DIRECT – Singlife Whole Life (lifelong protection). Both provide a lump-sum Death Benefit, with Terminal Illness and Total and Permanent Disability stated as early payouts of the Death Benefit. DIRECT – Singlife Term Life can cover you for as short as five years or up to age 65, with renewal details (maximum age to renew: 80; coverage up to age 85). It also states you can purchase optional critical illness coverage via a rider, providing a lump-sum if diagnosed with any of 30 covered critical illnesses, and that the rider accelerates the Death Benefit. Key limitation: DPI term life is described as having no cash value/savings.
quality_notes: The brochure contains some truncated/unfinished sentences (e.g., 'Premiums stay the same throughout the premium payment period, starting from:').
Many rider specifics (waiting period, exclusions, critical illness list) are referenced but not provided in this document; they are said to be in the Product Summary.
Premium amounts are given only as illustrations tied to specific assumptions rather than as general benefits or guaranteed rates.

The brochure highlights that this term product has no savings/investment feature (no cash value if it ends). extraction.document_summary: This Singlife brochure explains its Direct Purchase Insurance (DPI) life insurance offering, which can be bought directly online or at a customer service centre. It presents two independently selectable base products: DIRECT – Singlife Term Life (fixed-period coverage) and DIRECT – Singlife Whole Life (lifelong coverage). Both pay a lump-sum for death-related events, including death and early payouts for terminal illness and total and permanent disability, as described in the product notes. Coverage limits differ by product (term up to S$400,000; whole life up to S$200,000), and buyers choose payment frequency. Both products may also include an optional critical illness rider that provides a lump-sum for 30 covered critical illnesses but is explicitly described as accelerating the Death Benefit of the base policy. Eligibility is stated as Singapore residents aged 19 to 65 (age next birthday).
quality_notes: Brochure clearly distinguishes DIRECT – Singlife Term Life vs DIRECT – Singlife Whole Life and provides key limits and coverage scope.
Many detailed rider benefit rules (waiting periods/exclusions) are referenced but not included in this document, so benefit-level exclusions/periods cannot be reliably extracted.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Elite Term II is a term life insurance plan designed to leave a lump-sum inheritance when the Life Assured dies or is diagnosed with terminal illness. The base product has two marketed payment structures: (1) “Singlife Elite Term II (Regular Pay)”, where premiums are paid regularly throughout the coverage term, and (2) “Singlife Elite Term II (Limited Pay)”, where you choose a premium term (e.g., 5 years, 10 years, up to age 65, or up to age 75) and you get a return of value if you outlive the coverage term via a “Longevity Reward” and if you surrender early via a “Surrender Benefit”. For Limited Pay held to age 99, it states a payout of 100% of total premiums paid for the base plan; it also states Surrender Benefit can be 30% (during the 3rd policy year onward until end of premium term) or 80% (from end of premium term onwards), after amounts owing to the insurer.
quality_notes: Document provides clear product naming, base coverage mechanics (die/terminal illness lump sum), and Limited Pay-specific longevity and surrender mechanics.
Medical underwriting requirements, free-look, grace period, and exact entry/max ages are not explicitly stated (except renewal age limits in the GRO note).
Rider details are listed by name, but full benefit mechanics for each rider are not included in this brochure section.

policies.quick_summary: Term life insurance with lump-sum payout on death or terminal illness; offered with Regular Pay and Limited Pay premium structures. Limited Pay adds Longevity Reward (100% of total base premiums paid at age 99 if held to end of term) and Surrender Benefit (30% of total base premiums paid from the 3rd policy year until end of premium term; 80% thereafter). Coverage duration options include 5/10 years, yearly intervals from the 11th year until age 85, and cover to age 99; renewal is automatic for 5-year/10-year terms subject to renewal conditions stated for GRO/GRO note. Conversion option exists into endowment or whole life without further medical underwriting (subject to conditions stated).

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Whole Life Choice is a whole life protection plan (Base Cover plus an Additional Cover) designed to provide lifelong coverage for death and Terminal Illness. The brochure states that on Terminal Illness diagnosis, the Terminal Illness Benefit is paid as an advance payment of the Death Benefit (less amounts owing), in a lump sum. The Base Cover also accumulates cash value and bonuses from the start of the third policy year. You can customise protection by choosing the Additional Cover amount as 100% / 200% / 300% / 400% of the Base Sum Assured, with the Additional Cover lasting until a selected Additional Cover Age (65, 70, 75, 80 or 85) and then reducing by 12.5% each year over eight years. Living features include a Life Stage Withdrawal Benefit (withdraw accumulated reversionary bonuses up to two times; subject to conditions), a Retrenchment Benefit (premium waiver up to 12 months after a waiting period and unemployment criteria), and an Income Payout Option that converts policy cash value to monthly payouts from age 65 or end of premium term (whichever is later). Eligible key milestones can also be used for a Guaranteed Extra Protection Option (no insurability; limited to 100% of Base Sum Assured / up to S$500,000).

The brochure states the premium examples and illustrative cash value amounts, but does not provide general product guarantee figures beyond the structural rules and some percentage/age/term selections.

policies.quick_summary: A Singlife whole life protection plan with lifelong death and Terminal Illness cover, cash value accumulation, and living benefits such as Life Stage Withdrawal, Retrenchment premium waiver, and an Income Payout option. It includes a Base Cover (lifetime) plus an Additional Cover that can be set at 100%/200%/300%/400% of Base Sum Assured and reduces after the selected Additional Cover Age (65/70/75/80/85). Other key features include the Guaranteed Extra Protection Option at certain life events (no insurability), and premium payment term choices (10/15/20/25 years or pay until age 65). Rely on the policy’s product summary for full benefit details of the attached riders.

policies.premium_payment_term_description: Choose from 10, 15, 20, or 25 years, or pay until age 65.
policies.bonuses_or_dividends: Base Cover accumulates guaranteed and non-guaranteed cash value; non-guaranteed cash value is accumulated via reversionary bonus (declared annually) and Terminal Bonus, depending on Participating Fund performance.
policy_termination_events: Conversion to Reduced Paid-Up (RPU) or Extended Term Insurance (ETI) makes the Life Stage Withdrawal Benefit not applicable (per Important notes).
important_caveats: Life Stage Withdrawal Benefit: can be exercised up to two times; application must be submitted within 90 days of the life stage event; option is subject to conditions and not applicable if the basic policy has been converted to Reduced Paid-Up (RPU) or Extended Term Insurance (ETI).
Life Stage Withdrawal Benefit: not applicable if the basic policy has been converted to RPU or ETI.

Retrenchment Benefit: available once per policy; waiver applies up to 12 months after involuntary unemployment for three consecutive months, subject to waiting period and exclusions in circumstances (e.g., retirement/resignation/known layoffs).

Guaranteed Extra Protection Option: limited total coverage under option to 100% of Base Sum Assured or up to a maximum of S$500,000 per life (whichever is lower), and is extended to standard life only.
Terminal Illness advance payment: Terminal Illness Benefit is paid as advance payment of the Death Benefit, less amounts owing.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Maternity Care is a Singapore Life (Singlife) single-premium, 3-year maternity plan designed to cover the mother and the child for expenses/financial assistance arising from pregnancy complications and newborn-related conditions. For the mother, it provides coverage for “Death” and specified “Pregnancy complications,” each with a cover limit of 100% of sum assured, plus “Hospital care” with a cover limit of 1% of sum assured for each day of hospitalisation, capped at up to 30 days (subject to a separate rule that the hospital care benefit ends when 30% of the sum assured is paid or when the contract term ends—whichever is earlier). For the child, it similarly covers death, congenital illnesses, and hospital care (1% per day up to 30 days), and adds coverage for severe neonatal jaundice outpatient phototherapy (1% per day up to 30 days), stem cell transplant surgery (50% of sum assured), and developmental delay (10% of sum assured). It is purchasable within the application pregnancy window (13 to 36 weeks) and subject to eligibility ages (18 to 45 ANB).
quality_notes: Benefit schedule includes many listed conditions but the payout limit row is partially formatted, requiring reliance on the clearly stated Important Notes for stem cell transplant (50% of sum assured) and developmental delay (10% of sum assured).
Some limit text for child benefits (e.g., stem cell treatment row) appears inconsistently formatted, so numeric parsing is supplemented by the Important Notes section.
Underwriting method/medical screening for the maternity plan itself is not stated; only the option to buy a new whole life plan for the child without medical underwriting is described.

policies.quick_summary: A single-premium 3-year maternity plan covering the mother and child for pregnancy complications, congenital illnesses, and hospitalisation-related expenses, with additional child benefits for outpatient phototherapy (severe neonatal jaundice), stem cell transplant surgery, and developmental delay. Mother/child “Death” and “Pregnancy complications/ Congenital illnesses” are covered at 100% of sum assured, while hospital/phototherapy care is covered at 1% of sum assured per day up to 30 days, subject to a hospital-care end rule for the mother (30% of sum assured paid or contract term ends). Child stem cell transplant pays 50% of sum assured; developmental delay pays 10% of sum assured.

The brochure states the policy has “no savings or investment feature”, and therefore there is no cash value if the policy ends or ends prematurely.

A separate option exists within 90 days from the birth of an insured child to buy a new whole life plan for the insured child without medical underwriting, subject to stated maximum total death/TI/TPD benefit amounts and a “pre-existing conditions” restriction.

extraction.document_summary: Singlife Cancer Cover Plus II is a cancer-focused medical insurance plan designed to protect against high out-of-pocket costs for cancer treatments worldwide, including treatments outside the Ministry of Health (MOH) Cancer Drug List (CDL). It provides “as-charged” protection for eligible cancer drug treatments and services, with a high annual coverage limit of up to S$1.5 million per policy year. The plan’s cost-sharing mechanism in the examples shows out-of-pocket spending as “20% of co-insurance + Monthly deductible,” with Singlife paying the remaining bill. It covers outpatient cancer drug treatments (on CDL and non-CDL), cancer drug services, and also Proton Beam Therapy plus Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy (with specific timing rules for related tests). Overseas treatment requires pre-approval and also imposes a prior-stay condition for Singapore residents.
quality_notes: Brochure states core product name, cancer-focused scope, coverage limit, and major benefit components (CDL/non-CDL outpatient drugs, drug services, Proton Beam Therapy, Cell/Tissue/Gene Therapy, and overseas treatment).
Key financial rule for cost-sharing is stated via examples and terminology definitions; exact deductible structure/amounts beyond examples are not fully specified in a standalone rule.
No explicit min/max entry ages, renewal terms, waiting periods, grace periods, or free-look period are stated.

The brochure includes detailed operational rules for overseas treatment pre-authorisation and timing windows for associated consultations/tests, as well as explicit non-coverage items (e.g., Class F non-CDL; experimental/pioneering/clinical trials).

policies.quick_summary: Cancer-focused medical plan with as-charged outpatient cancer drug treatment and services (on CDL and non-CDL), plus Proton Beam Therapy and Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy, and overseas coverage (subject to pre-authorisation and residency condition). Coverage limit up to S$1.5 million per policy year. Application via health questions with no medical check-up needed (per brochure). Cost-sharing in examples indicates out-of-pocket = 20% co-insurance + monthly deductible, then Singlife pays the remaining bill (as-charged). Non-CDL Class F is not covered; experimental/pioneering/clinical trials are not covered; follow-up after outpatient Proton Beam Therapy sessions is not covered.

coverage_scope: Outpatient cancer drug treatment listed on the MOH Cancer Drug List (CDL)
Outpatient cancer drug treatment for Non-CDL treatments under Classes A to E (Non-CDL framework)
Outpatient cancer drug services associated with cancer drug treatment (e.g., consultations, scans, lab investigations, preparation/administration, supportive care drugs, blood transfusions)

Proton Beam Therapy treatment as inpatient (including day surgery) or outpatient (associate consultation/tests allowed only if ordered before treatment and performed not more than 30 days before; follow-up after each outpatient session not covered)

Cell, Tissue and Gene Therapy treatment as inpatient or outpatient (subject to policy general exclusions; definition aligned with Health Products Act and excludes Immunotherapy as stated in brochure context)
Overseas treatment in an overseas hospital for covered cancer treatments, subject to residency condition and pre-authorisation certificate
policies.residency_requirements: Overseas treatment eligibility requires that the Life Assured had not stayed outside Singapore for more than 183 consecutive days within a 12-month period on or before admission date, and that Singlife pre-approves and issues a certificate of pre-authorisation.
policies.eligibility_notes: Sign-up by answering 3 simple health questions with no medical check-up needed (as stated).
important_caveats: Outpatient cancer drug treatments are only claimable if used according to the clinical indications specified on the CDL (as at the date of treatment), unless otherwise stated in the policy.
Non-CDL outpatient cancer drug treatment covers Classes A to E; Class F treatments are not covered.
For outpatient Proton Beam Therapy, follow-up consultation fees/exams/lab tests/other medical attention after each session are not covered.

Overseas treatment requires pre-approval and pre-authorisation, and the Life Assured must not have stayed outside Singapore for more than 183 consecutive days within a 12-months period on or before admission date.
This is stated as having no savings or investment feature; there is no cash value if policy ends or terminates prematurely.

extraction.document_summary:
Singlife Shield is an Integrated Shield Plan that provides enhanced hospitalisation coverage beyond MediShield Life for both public and private hospital treatment, with coverage options by ward type. The brochure states three base plans: Shield Plan 1 (A) covers “Private Hospital (any standard ward)” with a policy-year limit “Up to S$2 million”; Shield Plan 2 (A) covers “Public Hospital (any standard ward (A))” with limit “Up to S$1.2 million”; Shield Plan 3 (B) covers “Public Hospital (any 4-bed standard ward (B1))” with limit “Up to S$500,000”. It also describes pre-hospitalisation as-charged coverage up to 180 days and post-hospitalisation up to 365 days.

Singlife Health Plus is described as an add-on rider that reduces out-of-pocket costs and adds additional benefits. Under a private-hospital example, co-insurance can reduce from 10% (capped at S$25,500/year) to 5% (capped at S$6,000/year). Health Plus also includes outpatient cancer drug coverage on the CDL (stated as “Outpatient Cancer Drug Treatment on the CDL”) and adds other rider benefits such as Mental Wellness Benefit (after 10 months’ continuous cover) and the Singlife Care Collab Recovery Support Benefit (up to S$20,000 per lifetime, max 730 consecutive days). A key limitation noted is that “Class F treatments are not covered” under non-CDL outpatient cancer drug treatment.
quality_notes: The Markdown contains broken/garbled text in several places (e.g., headings and some lines around the plan tables).
Some fields (e.g., entry ages, exact co-insurance/deductible linkage for each plan, and underwriting/renewability) are not stated explicitly.
Despite garbling, the document clearly states major mechanics and multiple benefit limits/conditions, and provides explicit exclusions (Class F not covered).

policies.quick_summary: An Integrated Shield Plan providing enhanced hospitalisation coverage (A&E/preferred providers, pre- and post-hospital treatment) beyond MediShield Life, with base plan limits by ward/hospital type. The add-on rider Singlife Health Plus is used to reduce co-insurance (e.g., 10% capped vs 5% capped) and provides added outpatient cancer and other support benefits (e.g., Mental Wellness Benefit after 10 months; Recovery Support up to S$20,000/lifetime). Class F non-CDL outpatient cancer treatments are not covered under the non-CDL framework note in the brochure’s important notes section when referencing non-CDL classification.
coverage_scope: Enhanced hospitalisation coverage for public and private hospital treatments
A&E or preferred medical provider coverage mechanics
Pre-hospitalisation treatment up to 180 days before hospitalisation
Post-hospitalisation treatment up to 365 days after discharge
Outpatient cancer drug treatment (CDL and non-CDL) (as described in benefits table/notes)
Extra inpatient benefit for 5 critical illnesses (labeled in the plan benefits table)
Outpatient psychiatric consultation (Mental Wellness Benefit) (conditions/limits described in important notes)
important_caveats: This policy has no savings or investment feature; the brochure states there is no cash value if the policy ends or is terminated prematurely.
Outpatient cancer drug treatments under the non-CDL framework: “Class F treatments are not covered.”
Mental Wellness Benefit requires the policy be in force continuously for at least 10 months from the cover start date.
